targets.name: output-assembler
targets.rationale: The OUTPUT assembler is the schema-determined cut planner and serialiser behind the {frames + field-map} to JSON boundary. Its witness command includes unit, nested round-trip, documented nesting, v2 inference, and exact checkpoint-boundary contracts. The measured local survivor rate is 9.09% against the unchanged 10% ceiling after syntax-only annotation and keyword-marker exclusions; executable planner and assembly behavior remains in scope.

targets.name: jsonpath
targets.rationale: The single-sourced path-grammar core (PATH_GRAMMAR.md) — acceptance, canonicality, and the canonical writer. Both INPUT and OUTPUT depend on it, so subtle branch mutations are high-priority signal. Residual survivors are five equivalent mutants: '==' -> 'is' on single-char (interned) dispatch, '<' -> '!='/'is not' on a loop bound that never overshoots, and '==' -> '>=' on the canonical-writer round-trip (a canonical re-emit never lexically exceeds its input).

targets.name: json-shred
targets.rationale: The structured-input engine is the load-bearing JSON/JSONL/XML decomposition, bounded-spill, cache-publication, source-proof, cross-process-lock, and runtime-snapshot boundary. Its maintained 687-test mutation command combines eight focused modules with 362 exact selectors, while broader modules remain in ordinary CI. It exercises parser conservation, multi-port loading, native source revisions, direct spill limits, atomic prepare/commit/discard, recovery, concurrent locking, source invalidation, process ownership, and adversarial cleanup paths. Complete-inference witnesses additionally cover cache bounds and request sharing, strict shape-filter equivalence and fast-path acceptance at integer/array/depth boundaries, shared-prefix learning, fused-parser error parity, and exact record-size limits. The hosted plan calibrates the exact command under the unchanged 90-second ceiling before scheduling shards. The 5% survival ceiling remains unchanged as the module grows. Only proven-equivalent selection and syntax-only postponed annotations are excluded with reviewed pragmas; executable expressions and branch decisions remain mutation-tested.
